items.definition:
kickboxing
She trains in kickboxing three times a week.

lifesaver (something or someone that helps one in a difficult situation)
That extra coffee was a real lifesaver this morning.

marksman (a person who is skilled in shooting)
He was a marksman in the army, rarely missing his target.

millisecond (one thousandth of a second)
The computer processed the data in just a few milliseconds.

A person who attends a funeral or expresses sorrow for someone's death.
The mourners gathered at the graveside, dressed in black.

A person or company that sells clothes and equipment for a particular activity.
We bought all our camping gear from the local outfitter.

A narrow strip of territory projecting from a larger territory.
The Florida panhandle extends along the Gulf Coast.

A rich, savory paste made from meat, fish, or vegetables.
We spread the duck pate on crackers as an appetizer.

the house of a rector or parish priest
The new priest moved into the rectory last week.

the action or process of changing the way in which something is organized
The company underwent a major reorganisation.

a person or thing that rises; a vertical part of a stair
He's an early riser, always up before dawn.

a noisy disturbance or quarrel
The children caused quite a ruckus in the classroom.

a device that divides a signal or stream into multiple parts
We need a cable splitter to connect two TVs.

a large enclosed horse-drawn vehicle formerly used to carry passengers and mail
The old stagecoach rattled down the dusty road.

a man of exceptional physical strength; a political leader who rules with absolute power
The strongman lifted the heavy weights with ease.

a hard calcified deposit that forms on the teeth; a fierce or intractable person
The dentist removed the tartar from his teeth.

a book in which words are grouped according to similarity of meaning
I used a thesaurus to find a synonym for 'happy'.

birds that live on or near water
Many species of waterfowl can be found in this wetland.

a screen or image format wider than it is tall
The movie was presented in widescreen format.

An act of transporting supplies or people by aircraft.
An emergency airlift brought supplies to the isolated village.

An attractive but unintelligent young woman (often derogatory).
The character was portrayed as a stereotypical bimbo.

A self-sustaining process that proceeds without external help.
The startup managed to bootstrap its operations with minimal funding.

Meat cut from the breast of an animal, typically a cow.
Smoked brisket is a popular dish in Texas.

A solid metal ball fired from a cannon; or a dive into water where one hugs one's knees to one's chest.
The children loved doing a cannonball into the swimming pool.

a large French country house or castle
They spent their vacation touring an old French château.

a person from Cyprus
The Cypriot delegation arrived for the international conference.

a disturbance from a proper place
He suffered a shoulder dislocation during the game.

government issue; a US soldier
Many G.I.s returned home after the war.

a long, deep cut or wound
He had a deep gash on his arm from the fall.

a person who stares openly in a stupid or rude manner
The gawkers stood around the accident scene.

a woman employed to teach and train the children in a private household
The children's governess taught them French and piano.

a person whose sour, grumpy attitude spoils the pleasure of others
Don't be such a Grinch and try to enjoy the party.

a fight with guns
The old Western movie featured a dramatic gunfight.

a derogatory term for a person from a rural, mountainous area, especially in the southern US
The old man was often stereotyped as a hillbilly because of his accent and rural upbringing.

a stupid person
He called me an imbecile for forgetting my keys.

an act of pretending to be another person for entertainment or fraud
His impersonation of the celebrity was spot on.

a Japanese aircraft loaded with explosives and making a deliberate suicidal crash on an enemy target
During World War II, kamikaze pilots were used by Japan.

a large brown seaweed that typically has a long, tough stalk and a broad frond, forming large beds in the sea
Sea otters often wrap themselves in kelp to avoid drifting away while they sleep.

the series of changes in the life of an organism or object
Understanding the product lifecycle is crucial for business planning.

a person who studies linguistics or is skilled in foreign languages
The linguist analyzed the ancient text to understand its grammar.

a stringed musical instrument
The musician played a beautiful melody on the ancient lute.

a type of sheep or the fine wool from it
She bought a soft sweater made of merino wool.

a tiny wafer of semiconductor material used to make an integrated circuit
Every modern computer contains numerous microchips.

a marine mollusk or a type of submarine
The submarine in 'Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas' was called the Nautilus.

a mythological spirit of nature imagined as a beautiful maiden
The ancient Greeks believed that nymphs lived in forests and rivers.

an optical instrument used to view objects that are not in the direct line of sight
The submarine raised its periscope to scan the surface.

physical therapy
After the accident, she needed physiotherapy to regain strength in her leg.

natural coloring of animal or plant tissue
Skin pigmentation can be affected by sun exposure.

an introductory statement
The Constitution begins with a preamble outlining its purpose.

the state or condition of being engrossed in something
His main preoccupation was his upcoming exams.

a person who inflicts punishment
In some stories, the hero acts as a punisher of evil.

the action of reorganizing or restructuring
The company announced a major realignment of its departments.

a series of boat races
The annual rowing regatta attracts teams from all over the country.

a difficult, tiring effort
The last mile of the marathon was a real slog.

an expert in statistics
The statistician analyzed the survey results.

short, stiff hairs or stalks
He had a five o'clock shadow of stubble on his chin.

a secondary or subordinate system
The computer's cooling system is a crucial subsystem.

a person who cheats or deceives
The fox is often portrayed as a clever trickster in fables.

a small, inexpensive ornament
She collected little trinkets from all the places she visited.

strength, energy, enthusiasm
He tackled the project with renewed vigour.

a red, swollen mark on skin; a strip of material
The sting left a raised red welt on her arm.

the quality of being able to adjust to new conditions
Her adaptability made her a valuable team member.

the quality of being aggressive or hostile
His aggressiveness in negotiations helped secure the deal.

a ghost or ghostlike image of a person
She claimed to have seen an apparition in the old house.
